title: Smt. Johra Bi v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J. and Krishan Pahal, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5 Executive Engineer remedy.
headnote: A writ raising electricity grievances was dismissed because Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the appropriate remedy: a representation to the Executive Engineer. Merits were not decided.
facts: Smt. Johra Bi invoked the writ jurisdiction of the High Court at Allahabad against the State of Uttar Pradesh and another, through counsel Rajesh Kumar Mishra. The respondents appeared through the Chief Standing Counsel and Rajesh Yadav. Writ-C No. 24902 of 2021 was heard by a Division Bench of Sunita Agarwal and Krishan Pahal JJ. The order does not record the connection, billing, or assessment facts behind the grievances, or any prior representation to the licensee.

holding_units.topic: alternative remedy — representation to Executive Engineer
holding_units.holding: For grievances of the kind raised in the writ, the appropriate remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer by invoking Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy.

principle_tags.application: The Court held that the petitioner's grievances were to be taken to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 rather than in writ.
The writ was dismissed solely because Clause 6.5 supplied an alternative remedy.
Clause 6.5 was treated as the statutory forum for the grievances pressed.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioner's electricity grievances
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the underlying dispute or grant or refuse relief on the facts; dismissal rested only on alternative remedy under Clause 6.5.
